incidents.vector: Unauthenticated buffer-overflow zero-day (CVE-2026-0300, CVSS 9.3) in the PAN-OS User-ID Authentication Portal lets attackers run code as root by sending crafted packets to internet-exposed captive portals.
incidents.impact: Attackers achieved RCE on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls, deployed EarthWorm and ReverseSocks5 tunneling tools, conducted Active Directory enumeration with stolen service-account credentials, and systematically destroyed logs. CISA added the bug to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and ordered federal agencies to mitigate by Saturday; first patches expected May 13. Shadowserver counts 5,800+ exposed VM-Series instances.

incidents.victim: Instructure (Canvas LMS) and ~9,000 K-12 and higher-ed institutions
incidents.vector: Threat actor compromised credentials/access tokens to Canvas back-end systems and exfiltrated user records and stored messages; Canvas Data 2, Beta and Test environments were taken offline during incident response.
incidents.impact: ShinyHunters claims 3.65 TB exfiltrated covering ~275 million users — names, emails, student IDs and inter-user messages. Group posted a "PAY OR LEAK" deadline; Instructure rotated keys and revoked privileged credentials but said no passwords, dates of birth, government IDs or financial data were taken. Schools remain on the hook under FERPA.

incidents.vector: ClickFix-style social engineering: fake macOS troubleshooting blogs and Squarespace/Craft/Medium pages instruct users to paste a Terminal command that downloads and executes AppleScript or Bash loaders, bypassing Gatekeeper and notarization checks.
incidents.impact: Three parallel campaigns deploy Macsync, Shub Stealer and AMOS infostealers that harvest browser credentials, Keychain entries, iCloud data, Telegram artifacts, Notes and crypto wallet seeds, and trojanize Trezor Suite, Ledger Live and Exodus. A Russian/CIS keyboard kill-switch suggests Russian-speaking operators; staging directories use the marker "SHub".

incidents.vector: Activist group "Centurion Project" obtained Alberta's official list of electors — names, addresses and other personal details — through unauthorized possession; channel of acquisition is under criminal investigation.
incidents.impact: About three-fifths of Alberta's population had voter-roll data exposed amid an active push toward an independence referendum. Police are investigating the unauthorized possession; risk of voter targeting and intimidation is elevated.

incidents.victim: Linux systems worldwide (Ubuntu, Amazon Linux, RHEL, SUSE, Debian)
incidents.vector: Deterministic local privilege escalation (CVE-2026-31431, dubbed "Copy Fail") in the Linux kernel's algif_aead AF_ALG interface; a 732-byte Python script reliably overwrites four bytes in the page cache to inject root shellcode into setuid binaries like /usr/bin/su.
incidents.impact: Affects every major Linux distribution since 2017 (kernels 4.14–6.19.12), enabling container/Kubernetes escapes, multi-tenant host takeover, and CI/CD pipeline compromise without touching disk. CISA warned that exploitation has begun in the wild; the modification leaves no on-disk forensic trace.

incidents.victim: Government entities in South America and southeastern Europe
incidents.vector: China-nexus APT "UAT-8302" gains initial access (likely zero-/n-day exploitation), then pivots with Impacket, custom PowerShell recon scripts, and a portfolio of malware including NetDraft (a .NET FinalDraft/SquidDoor variant), CloudSorcerer v3, VSHELL/SNOWLIGHT, the Rust-based SNOWRUST stager and Draculoader.
incidents.impact: Talos assesses with high confidence the actor is tasked with long-term access for espionage. Tooling overlaps with Jewelbug/REF7707, Earth Estries, Earth Naga and UNC5174, indicating shared resourcing across China-nexus clusters. Active in S. America since late 2024 and SE Europe through 2025.

incidents.victim: Microsoft Windows / SharePoint customers (167 CVEs patched)
incidents.vector: Patch Tuesday addressed 167 vulnerabilities; CVE-2026-32201 (SharePoint Server spoofing, actively exploited) lets attackers present falsified content within trusted SharePoint environments, and CVE-2026-33825 ("BlueHammer") is a publicly disclosed Windows Defender privilege-escalation flaw.
incidents.impact: Active SharePoint exploitation enables phishing, unauthorized data manipulation and social engineering against partners and customers. Adobe Reader and Chrome (4th 2026 zero-day) also received emergency patches the same week, including an actively exploited Reader RCE.

incidents.victim: Municipal water and drainage utility, Monterrey, Mexico
incidents.vector: Threat actor used a frontier AI model to perform substantial portions of the intrusion against the utility's network, per incident-response findings reported by Dragos.
incidents.impact: First publicly disclosed case of an AI-driven compromise of a North American municipal water provider; details on access scope and operational impact are still emerging. CISA cited cases like this when launching its CI Fortify initiative this week.

incidents.vector: DDoS-for-hire service launched a sustained volumetric attack against Canonical's server infrastructure; the service claims peaks above 3.5 Tbps.
incidents.impact: Ubuntu installation and update services have been intermittently unavailable since the start of the campaign. Disruption affects developers and downstream Linux distributions that pull from Canonical mirrors. Attribution beyond the for-hire service has not been published.

incidents.victim: Ethnic Korean community in Yanbian, China
incidents.attacker: North Korea — state-sponsored (Ministry of State Security)
incidents.vector: APT37 compromised the website of Chinese game developer Sqgame and pushed a malicious update package to its Android card-game suite; victims sideloaded the games outside Google Play and received the "BirdCall" backdoor via the update.
incidents.impact: BirdCall captures contacts, SMS, call logs, microphone audio, screenshots, media files and private keys; ESET found seven Android variants developed since at least November 2024. The campaign appears to target North Korean defectors and refugees in the China–DPRK border region.

incidents.vector: A student used software-defined radio (SDR) and handheld radios to transmit a forged high-priority "General Alarm" signal on the rail-control radio frequency, forcing emergency-braking procedures.
incidents.impact: Four trains were halted for 48 minutes. No injuries reported but the case underscores rail-radio integrity weaknesses that could be replicated by more capable adversaries; local authorities are pursuing charges.

incidents.vector: Threat actor gained unauthorized access to a portion of Trellix's source-code repository; method and entry point not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Source-code exposure for a security vendor risks revealing where controls are placed and how detections are designed, providing follow-on attackers a roadmap. Trellix says its release/distribution pipeline was not affected and engaged forensic experts and law enforcement; latest in a string of supply-chain hits on security vendors after F5 (2025) and the TeamPCP campaign against Trivy and KICS earlier this year.

incidents.victim: UAE critical-business sectors (finance, telecom, aviation, law enforcement, energy-adjacent)
incidents.vector: Iran-aligned hacktivists, opportunistic cybercriminals and state actors mobilized after the start of the 2026 Israel/US–Iran conflict, focusing on identity systems, payment processing, port logistics, aviation and cloud-dependent government services rather than headline DDoS.
incidents.impact: Daily UAE breach attempts climbed from 90,000–200,000 pre-conflict to 600,000–800,000; UAE "cyber-relevant activity" rose 15x, Saudi Arabia 25x, Qatar 4x. CypherLeak found no successful destructive infrastructure attacks yet, but the UAE Cyber Security Council says the baseline has shifted upward and may persist as the new normal.

incidents.victim: Brazilian ISPs and small regional providers
incidents.vector: Threat actor with root access to Huge Networks infrastructure used CEO SSH keys plus a Mirai-variant botnet of TP-Link Archer AX21 routers (vulnerable to CVE-2023-1389) and open DNS resolvers to launch coordinated DNS reflection/amplification DDoS campaigns.
incidents.impact: Targeted Brazilian IP ranges in 10–60 second bursts with four parallel processes per host. Huge Networks' CEO blames a January 2026 intrusion of two dev servers and a personal droplet, claiming a competitor framed the company; pattern matches a longstanding template of DDoS-mitigation firms running attacks to drum up business. Investigation by third-party forensics ongoing.

incidents.victim: Government, scientific, manufacturing and retail organizations in Russia, Belarus and Thailand
incidents.vector: Supply-chain compromise of DAEMON Tools Lite (versions 12.5.0.2421–2434): legitimately signed installers shipped a backdoor that profiled hosts, then pushed the QUIC RAT only to selected high-value targets.
incidents.impact: Several thousand machines across 100+ countries received the basic implant; a dozen targeted victims received QUIC RAT, including an unidentified Russian educational institution. Kaspersky says Chinese-language artifacts indicate a Chinese-speaking actor. Disc Soft says it remediated within 12 hours of disclosure but the campaign began April 8 and remained active for nearly a month.

incidents.vector: Threat actor targeted DigiCert's support team with a malicious payload disguised as a screenshot delivered via the customer chat channel, compromising the support portal.
incidents.impact: DigiCert revoked an unspecified set of certificates after detecting the breach. As a top global CA, any compromise of issuance or support infrastructure has cascading trust implications for TLS and code-signing customers worldwide; full scope still being assessed.
